newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-ANFIELD SURVIVORS PSG TURN ATTENTION HOME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANFIELD SURVIVORS PSG TURN ATTENTION HOME.

text.p: European Cup Winners' Cup holders Paris St Germain must quickly recover from the ardours of their semifinal survival at Anfield to defend their second place in the French league at home to Nice on Sunday.
If Monaco beat Marseille on Saturday and PSG lose on Sunday, Monaco will be champions.

On paper the task against Nice ought not to put the Paris club under anything like the pressure they withstood in a 2-0 defeat by Liverpool which saw them edge into the Rotterdam final against Barcelona 3-2 on aggregate on Thursday.
Nice have not won in their last 11 matches, a record they share with fellow relegation candidates Caen and Nancy.
But the Parisians have confused friend and foe alike this season with their European resilience and domestic fragility, especially against the lower-placed sides, while Nice have nothing to lose.

The Cote d'Azur club are bottom of the first division with 10 points fewer than the side immediately above them, Nancy, and have been all but relegated, though they have redeemed their season with a place in the French Cup final at PSG's Parc des Princes stadium on May 10.
"It's a match with nothing at stake for us. Paris will be very motivated because they want to keep their second place in the championship," coach Silvester Takac said.

"It will be very hard to win against such a team who showed they are hard to beat at Liverpool, withstanding the rhythm that was imposed on them there. For us it's a question of preparing for the cup final."
He added that Nice face the challenge of showing they are a better team than their dismal league record this season shows and that they are worthy cup finalists.
Midfielder Frederic Tatarian said: "Curiously, it's a match between two cup finalists...We'll be relaxed... As Paris spent a lot of energy at Liverpool, why not try to surprise them?"

Nice have decided to leave key defender Olivier Fugen on the bench for fear of losing him for the cup final through suspension if he picks up a booking at the Parc on Sunday. He is also suffering from back pains.
They are also without goalkeeper Bruno Valencony, who is nursing a thigh injury and will be replaced by Robin Huc.
But Nice welcome back midfielder Roberto Onorati after a long injury lay-off and the Italian is keen to play himself into the cup final side.
Liberian striker James Debbah is still unavailable with an eye injury but he is optimistic he will play in the final.
PSG will be without suspended defender Laurent Fournier, while striker Julio Cesar Dely Valdes is still unavailable after flying home to Panama after the sudden death of his sister.
But PSG should manage to maintain defensive balance with the return from injury of Didier Domi.
